_: MT-007 — capabilities the workflow in core/ uses that a given AI tool may not have, how to detect each use in core content, and what to do without it. scripts/generate-workflow-manual.js renders core/skills and core/agents into plain step-by-step playbooks for a tool that has none of them, appending the fallbacks each skill needs. Every capability core uses must be listed here; npm run check fails otherwise.

capabilities.without: There is no argument variable: read the task id or topic the person gave you in their message, and use it wherever this playbook says <argument>.
Nothing runs before you start reading. Run each command marked "Run first" yourself, in the project root, and read its output before continuing.

Do the delegated step yourself, serially, in this same session: open the matching playbook under agents/ and follow it with exactly the inputs this step names. Keep what it asks you to read to what it lists — the delegation existed to keep that context small.

There is no built-in reviewer. Read the diff yourself (git diff main...HEAD) once for bugs — off-by-one, null/undefined, error paths, races — and once for security if it touches auth, input handling, files, SQL or secrets. Report findings the way the step describes.
Rules are not loaded for you when you touch a file. Before editing, open rules/ and read every rule whose paths match the files you are about to change.

Nothing blocks a forbidden edit or command during the session. Check .claude/stack.json "protected" before editing a file, never bypass git hooks, and run node .claude/gate.js before pushing — the gate is the same rules enforced outside the session.
There is one model. Ignore the tier; the playbook works the same, only slower or more expensive.

guarantees.note: gate.js runs verify from the pre-push hook and CI, so it holds whatever tool wrote the code.
audit and secrets steps of the gate, per auditMode/secretsMode.
requirement coverage, security baseline, supply chain, operational readiness, budgets and evals run in the gate when their files exist.
guard-bash and the settings deny list stop it inside a Claude Code session only. Outside one, only branch protection on the git host stops it — which is the host's setting, not the kit's.
guard-edit blocks the edit inside a session. The gate cannot tell who changed a file, so a protected file edited by another tool is not caught; review is the only remaining check.
guard-edit only. Outside a session, review the diff of test files on fix/ and hotfix/ branches by hand.
guard-bash blocks --no-verify inside a session; outside, CI running the same gate is what catches a bypassed pre-push.
